subject: Request: multi-year prepay - ramp exception & discount approval
messages:
From: Anna Klein <anna.klein@cedarbrook.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-04T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood proposal - multi-year prepay request

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Cedarbrook is very keen to lock in capacity for our AI initiatives — we run a heavier tail on embeddings and expect steady growth. Procurement asked me to send the specifics so you can route for approvals. High-level ask:

- Term: 3 years (annual invoices, paid upfront each year)
- Yearly committed spend: Year1 $300k, Year2 $450k, Year3 $1.2M (total $1.95M)
- Discount: requesting 40% off list for committed usage (we know this is high; we want to make the economics work given the long-term guarantee)
- Ramp exception: allow credits to roll forward for unmet commit in Year1 up to 50% of Year1 commit; allow refund up to 25% if usage < 50% of commit in Year1
- Other asks: SOC2 evidence, on-prem connector SLAs, 30-day termination rights for failure to meet key KPIs

Attached is a short term request from our procurement team (Cedarbrook_term_request.pdf). If possible, we can do a call with finance/legal this week to move quickly — Cedarbrook procurement is targeting signature by Dec 15.

Best,
Anna Klein
Sourcing Lead, Cedarbrook Systems
anna.klein@cedarbrook.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Klein <anna.klein@cedarbrook.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-04T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal - multi-year prepay request

Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the term summary. I appreciate the timeline.

Quick notes:
- We can move this through, but the discount and the refund/large roll-forward request are non-standard and will require signoff from Sales leadership, Finance, and Legal.
- I'll loop in Marcus (sales lead) and Neha (finance) for commercial boundaries, and Aditya for legal redline expectations.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow for a final commercial alignment before we put a counter in writing? If Dec 15 is firm on your side, we should lock terms this week.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-04T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: FWD: Redwood proposal - multi-year prepay request — Cedarbrook (escalation)

Team — forwarding Cedarbrook's request (attached). Key items and questions below:

Cedarbrook asks: 3-year prepay with a lumpy ramp (20%/23%/57% of total across years), ~40% discount on committed usage, large roll-forward allowance (50% of Year1) and refund cap request (25% Year1). They want signature target Dec 15.

What I need from you:
- Marcus: recommended counter (discount cap we can offer without exec uplift) and commercial rationale for pushing back on refunds vs credits.
- Neha: finance modeling — what incremental margin/coverage do we need to accept >30% discount? Can we structure tranche-based payouts or escrow?
- Aditya: legal must confirm whether we can accept the requested refund language and what limited liability/termination changes would be required.
- Stephanie: FYI — this is a strategic prospect in our banking vertical; your guidance on go/no-go for aggressive pricing would help.

Attachments: Cedarbrook_term_request.pdf. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/rdw-2398

I'll hold off on a written counter until we align.

– Laura
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-05T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Cedarbrook (escalation)

Quick take from Sales:
- I can approve up to 30% list discount for a 3-year committed relationship provided we eliminate refunds and convert to credit roll-forward with a 12-month expiry.
- For anything above 30% we need VP Sales approval (Stephanie). For 35%+ we'd also want a co-sell/marketing commitment and an exec intro to their board to justify deeper discount.
- Recommend counter: 30% on committed usage, quarterly true-ups, credits roll for up to 4 quarters only, no cash refunds. Offer a one-time onboarding credit to help Year1 absorb spike.

Rationale: this preserves revenue while giving Cedarbrook flexibility; refunds materially increase churn risk and accounting complexity.

– Marcus
Director, Enterprise Sales
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-05T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Cedarbrook (escalation) — finance modeling

Attached (usage-modeling.xlsx) with simple P&L for the proposed ramp. Short summary:
- At 40% discount effective across the commit, expected gross margin drops below 28% for Year1 which is below our acceptable threshold for reserved capacity deals.
- If the customer pre-pays Year1 in full and we get a binding commitment (no refunds), we can push to ~34% margin if we amortize onboarding and the larger portion of Year3.
- Allowing cash refunds in Year1 (as requested) materially increases bad-debt and recognition complexity; from an accounting + cashflow perspective, credits (12mo rollover) are far preferable.

Options to enable a higher discount without hurting margin:
1) Require full Year1 prepay and reduce refund to 0% (credits only) — allowable discount up to 35% with CFO signoff.
2) If we must allow a refund, cap it at 10% of Year1 and require evidence of usage and quarterly true-ups — allowable discount up to 30%.

If leadership wants to go to 40% we need explicit CFO (Rishi) approval and additional commercial protections (performance-linked ramp, reduced SLA credits).

– Neha
Head of Finance, Enterprise
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Klein <anna.klein@cedarbrook.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-06T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Redwood proposal - multi-year prepay request

Anna — thanks for patience while we ran this up internally. Below is our commercial counter (we can finalize legal wording after commercial alignment):

Counter (commercial):
- Term: 3 years; annual invoices paid at start of each year (prepay preferred).
- Commit: As discussed.
- Discount: 32% off list on committed usage (effective across the three-year commit) — this is our best commercial offer without VP Sales/CFO escalation.
- Refunds / roll-forward: No cash refunds. We will allow credits to roll forward up to 12 months for unmet commit in Year1 only; thereafter credits expire.
- True-ups: Quarterly consumption true-ups.
- Legal & SLAs: We will provide SOC2 evidence and a standard enterprise SLA; termination for convenience limited, termination for material breach preserved.

Attachments: Redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf (term summary), usage-modeling.xlsx (finance).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of credits vs refunds.
2) If accepted, we'll have Legal (Aditya) prepare the redline and route to DocuSign. We can propose a short exec call (LA/Marcus/Neha + Cedarbrook procurement) if you want to accelerate.

If Cedarbrook requires >32% discount or cash refunds, we'll need VP Sales/CFO approval and will require additional protections (performance-linked ramps, higher minimums).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

- No cash refunds; acceptance of credit rollover is critical for our procurement team.
- Request a 1-week turnaround on legal redlines and a DocuSign link so procurement can finalize before Dec 15.

We appreciate the flexibility — please have Aditya send the redline and the DocuSign envelope. I'll coordinate internally to accelerate.
